newsitem.title: USA: Smith's Food to take Q1 charge $25 million.
newsitem.headline: Smith's Food to take Q1 charge $25 million.

text.p: Smith's Food & Drug Centers Inc said on Thursday it will take an extraordinary, after-tax charge of about $25 million in the first quarter of 1997 from writing off deferred financing costs.

Smith's said it has completed arrangements with Chase Manhattan Corp and Bankers Trust New York Corp for term loans totaling $600 million and a $150 million revolving credit facility, less amounts outstanding under letters of credit.
Proceeds from the refinancing will be used to pay off existing debt, effectively reducing the company's interest-rate costs by $11 million per year, Smith's said.
After taking the $25 million charge, future amortization of deferred financing costs will be reduced by about $5.5 million per year, the company said.
Smith's shares were holding at 34-1/2 early Thursday, unchanged on the day.

Smith's operates 150 supermarkets in western states. It reported a full-year 1996 loss of $164.1 million, or $8.42 per share, on revenues of $2.9 billion. But its fourth-quarter 1996 results showed a profit of $0.48 per share, compared to a loss of $2.79 per share for the same period the year before.
